title: Pre-Analysis — Bonding and Inlet Screen Change for the Centre Tank Boost Pump Canisters
abstract: Pre-analysis of a safety-driven bonding and inlet screen change on the centre tank boost pump canisters, returned for re-scoping when the bonding lead route and the ground point documentation were found to be outside the proposal.

sections.objective: Assess a proposal to add a bonding lead to the centre tank boost pump canisters and to change the inlet screen, raised against a fuel tank safety review rather than against a service finding. The proposal as submitted covered the canister and the screen only. Pre-analysis was asked whether that boundary is defensible, given that a bonding lead is only as good as the ground point it terminates on and that neither the ground point nor the lead route appeared anywhere in the submission.
sections.findings_summary: Two items were confirmed and they were enough to send the proposal back. The bonding lead has to terminate somewhere, and the wiring documentation that carries ground point definitions for the cabin floor and wing junction area contains no ground point in the canister bay at all; the proposal therefore either creates a new ground point, which is design work it does not include, or terminates on structure, which the safety review is unlikely to accept. Separately, a cargo compartment airflow and detection change raised in the same period was found by the descriptive text alone, sharing no identifier: it is the other half of the same fuel and fire safety review, and the two proposals were being assessed by different offices with no visibility of each other. The screen change itself raised no findings.
sections.next_steps: Return the proposal for re-scoping with the bonding lead route and the ground point definition included, and ask the electrical installation office to own that part rather than leaving it inside a fuel systems submission. Ask the safety review secretariat to list every proposal it has generated so that the two halves are assessed together. Re-raise the pre-analysis when the enlarged scope is available; the inlet screen change may be released separately if the operators want it sooner.

similarity_seeds: bonding resistance on a fuel tank pump canister
ground point definition for a new bonding lead
fuel and fire safety review generating parallel proposals

tasks.title: Trace the proposed bonding lead to a defined ground point
Search for other proposals from the same safety review
Assess the inlet screen change on its own

evidence.similarity_note: Reached from the description of the bonding lead rather than from any identifier. The wiring sheet is the ground point authority for the cabin floor and wing junction area and shares no part number, functional item number or zone with the pump canister installation.

expected_findings.rationale: A bonding lead is defined by its termination. The ground point list contains no point in the canister bay, so the proposal as written either creates one, which is design work it does not include, or terminates on structure, which the safety review will not accept.
expected_findings.resolution: Return the proposal with the lead route and ground point definition inside its scope, owned by the electrical installation office.

evidence.similarity_note: Found only by the descriptive text. One proposal speaks of bonding resistance and inlet screens on fuel pump canisters, the other of airflow compensation and detector sensitivity in the cargo compartment. No part number, functional item number, drawing or zone is shared, and the two sit in different chapters with different design offices.

expected_findings.rationale: Both proposals were generated by the same fuel and fire safety review and are being assessed in isolation. Whatever is decided on one changes the argument for the other.
expected_findings.resolution: Ask the safety review secretariat for the full list of proposals it generated and assess them together.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with a negative position on the proposal as submitted. The bonding change cannot be assessed without its ground point, and the second half of the same safety review was being handled elsewhere.
